# zstd (built from source) — Provenance & Supply-Chain

`zstd` in this directory is **built in-tree from vendored upstream source** via
`BUILD_EXECUTABLE` (`Android.mk`), mirroring the sibling `pigz` module. It is the
compressor the TWRP recovery backup/restore pipeline drives (`execlp("zstd", …)`,
multi-pipe, `-T<N>`). The former opaque prebuilt blob has been removed.

## Updating

Run the updater from the working-dir root (needs network; downloads from GitHub):

```sh
Tools/update_zstd.sh            # vendor the latest STABLE release
Tools/update_zstd.sh v1.5.7     # pin / reproduce a specific tag
```

It fetches the release tarball **and** the upstream `.sha256` sidecar, verifies
with `sha256sum -c` (hard abort on mismatch), then refreshes `lib/` + `programs/`
+ `LICENSE`, rewrites `VERSION`, and regenerates the table above. `Android.mk`
needs no edit on a version bump (source lists use `all-c-files-under`).

A version bump is a deliberate change: review the diff and run it through the
project backup + changelog workflow before building.

## What is vendored

- `lib/common`, `lib/compress`, `lib/decompress`, `lib/dictBuilder`,
  `lib/deprecated` — the full `libzstd` source minus the legacy decoder.
- `programs/` — the CLI front-end (single `main()` in `programs/zstdcli.c`).
- `LICENSE` — upstream dual BSD / GPLv2.

Stripped by the updater (never compiled): `lib/legacy` (we build with
`-DZSTD_LEGACY_SUPPORT=0`) and `lib/dll` (Windows example dir). The x86_64-only
`lib/decompress/huf_decompress_amd64.S` is present but not listed in `Android.mk`
(arm/arm64 uses the portable C decoder; `-DZSTD_DISABLE_ASM=1`).

## Build flags

See the header comment in `Android.mk`. The load-bearing ones:
`-DZSTD_MULTITHREAD` (required for `-T<N>`), `-DBACKTRACE_ENABLE=0` (Bionic has no
`<execinfo.h>`), `-DZSTD_LEGACY_SUPPORT=0`, `-DZSTD_DISABLE_ASM=1`,
`-DXXH_NAMESPACE=ZSTD_`.

## SIMD / NEON

NEON needs **no flag** — it is already on. zstd gates its ARM NEON code on
`__ARM_NEON` (`lib/common/compiler.h`), which the AOSP clang defines for every
`aarch64` target (NEON is mandatory in AArch64). `-DZSTD_DISABLE_ASM=1` only gates
the x86_64 BMI2 `.S` assembly, **not** NEON; `ZSTD_NO_INTRINSICS` (which would turn
SIMD off) is deliberately not set.

Caveat on actual benefit: the NEON-accelerated path is the **row match finder**
(`lib/compress/zstd_lazy.c`), used only at compression level **>= ~5**. The default
backup level is **1** (`ZSTD_fast`, scalar), so the NEON code is compiled in but not
on the hot path. There is no aarch64 build flag that accelerates level 1 further;
warming NEON means raising `tw_zstd_level` (a throughput-for-ratio trade).

## Verify the built binary on device

```sh
zstd --version          # -> *** zstd command line interface ... v1.5.7
echo test | zstd -T4 -c | zstd -d -c   # multithread path must work, not error
```
